summary: Chamath argues the antitrust ruling removes a major risk overhang for Google, freeing it to compete aggressively in the AI era, while the judge's logic that the free market is already delivering competition is vindicated.
quote: The great news for Google is that this takes an enormous risk off the table. And now I think that they probably have even more ambition and energy to just go for it and try to compete.

summary: Sacks reversed his prior pro-breakup stance, now seeing Google as facing a genuine existential threat from AI substituting for search — not needing to be broken up but still needing to execute a major pivot as its core business is being disrupted.
quote: Google for the first time in a long while is existentially threatened by what's happened with AI. I mean, their cash cow, the core of their business is search, and people are starting to substitute in droves from traditional Google

summary: Sacks notes that roughly 90% of AI revenue is flowing to OpenAI, giving it dominant consumer position in the AI chatbot market that is displacing traditional search.
quote: If you look at AI revenue, I think something like 90% of it is going to OpenAI. I mean, they have the dominant position among consumers for now.
